title: Dance hall prices, packed ballrooms and WJR broadcasts from the Graystone
summary: Admission was 50 to 75 cents, McKinney's band packed every hall, and radio broadcasts from Detroit were the best publicity.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: How much was a dance hall? How much did it cost to get in to dance in those days?
75, you know. It's according to the band.
You would have to have at least a thousand people to have a good night.

Oh, sure, but they always had a good night. In those days when McKinney's band played anyplace it was packed all the time, every place you played. In fact, there were so many ballrooms over the country in those days, you see, --
Yes, didn't have radio and there was no television. It was just radio.
Just radio, and we used to broadcast. When we'd be in the Graystone, you know, which we would go in there and stay for weeks and months, we would broadcast over
WJR all the time, you see.
Uh-huh, yeah, yeah. We used to broadcast over WJR and that's what you had. That was the greatest publicity in the world right there is to be on the radio.
